newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Alumax looks to build plant in Venezuela.
newsitem.headline: Alumax looks to build plant in Venezuela.

text.p: U.S. aluminum company Alumax Inc is negotiating power and primary material supply contracts with an eye to building an aluminum plant in Venezuela with a capacity of 320,000 metric tonnes per year, a top government official said.

"There are official negotiations for basic supplies. I would say that it should be known in the first half of this year whether the project is viable," Elias Ynaty, president of state holding company Corporacion Venezolana de Guyana (CVG) told reporters.
Ynaty said the Alumax project was larger than an original plan to build a 60,000 metric tonnes per year plant which could later be increased to 120,000 metric tonnes per year.
"It is a more ambitious project than the original one which was worth about $600 million," he said.

Alumax had registered interest in the forthcoming privatization of Venezuela's four-company aluminum sector but pulled out and decided to revive the project it first presented to the CVG about a year ago, Ynaty said.
